teaser.text: Teradyne sells machines and software that test chips and electronic products, along with robots that move materials or perform factory work. Its business is easiest to understand as a chain: it builds a tool, a customer uses it to make or inspect something, and money flows in through equipment, services and continuing demand.

blocks.heading: What has to go right for Teradyne, and what could go wrong?

paragraphs.text: The bear case depends on customers absorbing capacity and utilization weakening. The bull case requires AI and memory ramps, production wins and stronger robotics execution. The outcome turns on qualified compute programs reaching volume, customers needing new tester capacity, and robotics producing repeat deployments rather than channel shipments alone.

blocks.heading: How much cash does Teradyne really make?

paragraphs.text: Free cash flow subtracts capital spending from operating cash. Teradyne used $224.0 million for property, plant and equipment in 2025 as it prepared for Semiconductor Test capacity needs. Stock compensation was $64.0 million: it is not a current cash payment, but it can dilute owners, so subtracting it produces a stricter measure of cash available to them.

blocks.heading: What does an investor pay for Teradyne today?

paragraphs.text: P/E, or price-to-earnings ratio, divides the share price by company profit. Trailing P/E uses the last twelve months of earnings, while forward P/E uses an estimate. A large one-time customer order can make profit jump and make P/E look cheap even though normal earning power has not changed. “Through-cycle” analysis asks what profits look like across strong and weak periods. That matters because Teradyne reported record revenue in the second quarter of 2026 as artificial-intelligence demand strengthened.

dividend.title: Teradyne dividend: is it covered by cash?
dividend.meta_description: Teradyne's dividend history, cash coverage, possible changes and yield are explained in plain English.
dividend.opening: Teradyne’s dividend is $0.52 per share on the current run rate; the forecast ranges from $0.48 to $0.72 per share. In 2025, Teradyne paid dividends and buybacks equal to 172.8% of free cash flow, so its shareholder payouts were not covered by that year’s free cash flow alone.
dividend.closing: The full Teradyne memo also answers how Teradyne’s business works, who its rivals are, how management allocates capital, and what risks could change the outlook.

blocks.heading: How much does Teradyne pay per share over time?

paragraphs.text: Dividends rise from $0.52 per share to $0.60 in the base case. That repeats the recent $0.04 annual step from $0.48 to the current $0.52 run rate. The bear case cuts the dividend to $0.48 after October 2027, while the bull case reaches $0.72 as cash generation strengthens. The board retains discretion, so neither path is guidance.

blocks.heading: Does Teradyne’s cash cover its dividend?

paragraphs.text: The company returned more cash to shareholders than that year’s free cash flow in 2025. Dividends and buybacks were 172.8% of free cash flow, and buybacks alone were $702,095 thousand. That meant Teradyne used accumulated cash or borrowing, rather than relying only on that year’s earnings power. Such a policy can be sensible if the shares are undervalued, but the cash-flow figures alone cannot show whether the repurchases created value.

paragraphs.text: Teradyne also spent on equipment and acquisitions, issued debt and ended 2025 with net cash. Its cash reserve was nevertheless much smaller than in 2021. Management has said it wants to reinvest, preserve reserves and retain capacity for acquisitions; the payout record shows that these aims compete for the same pool of money.

paragraphs.text: Dividend yield describes the dividend at a particular share price, not the full shareholder return. Cash, debt and capital allocation must therefore be read together.

blocks.heading: What has Teradyne's last eight quarters shown?

paragraphs.text: The sequence matters more than the single comparison. Revenue accelerated from weak mid-2025 quarters into late 2025 and the first half of 2026, with Semiconductor Test supplying most of the total. Cash flow also moved sharply between quarters because collections and other working-capital movements do not arrive evenly. The next question is whether customers need new capacity or can use what they already own.

blocks.heading: What should Teradyne watch after the next results?

paragraphs.text: The September-quarter results are scheduled by one estimate service for October 27, 2026, though that date is estimated. Investors should examine whether revenue and EPS land within the guide, whether product mix affects gross margin, and whether new-product launches bring the costs management described. Because the Q3 analyst sample is small, the company’s actual results and explanation matter more than a narrow consensus beat.

The larger checkpoint is the Q4 earnings call, when management has said it will update its target earnings model. This is a financial blueprint: expected revenue growth, margins, operating costs, investment, and resulting earnings. It becomes more credible when its assumptions connect to customer orders and capacity plans. A higher revenue target means less if it requires permanently higher costs or lower margins.
